name: Genubath
title: Son of Hadad from Edom
summary: Genubath was the son of Hadad, an Edomite prince who fled to Egypt after Joab had destroyed all the male Edomites. His mother was the sister of Queen Tahpenes of Egypt. Genubath was raised in Pharaoh's house among Pharaoh's own sons.

keyEvents.title: Hadad's Flight to Egypt
keyEvents.description: After Joab and the Israelites had killed all the male Edomites, Hadad fled as a young boy to Egypt, where Pharaoh welcomed him and gave him a house, food, and land.

keyEvents.title: Hadad Marries the Queen's Sister
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh gave Hadad the sister of his queen Tahpenes as a wife, which showed the high status Hadad received at the Egyptian court.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Genubath
keyEvents.description: Tahpenes' sister bore Genubath to Hadad, and Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh's house, where he grew up among Pharaoh's own sons.

keyEvents.title: Hadad Wishes to Return to Edom
keyEvents.description: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he asked Pharaoh to let him return to his own land, which was part of God's plan to raise up adversaries against Solomon.

keyEvents.title: Hadad as God's Adversary Against Solomon
keyEvents.description: The Lord raised up Hadad as an adversary against Solomon because of Solomon's sin in turning to other gods. This was part of God's judgment on Solomon's unfaithfulness.
